findings.description: `removeGateDir` now has to create a new directory before it can delete anything. If the temp filesystem is full (ENOSPC, or EDQUOT for an inode or quota limit), `mkdtempSync` throws. The catch then reports "Could not remove … (ENOSPC); it is left behind." and nothing is freed. Before this change, `rmSync` freed the space in exactly this case. A full temp volume is a realistic way for a gate run to end, for example a runaway test or build writing into scratch. The space is now never reclaimed, so the next `pup merge` fails at its own `mkdtempSync` (`pup-gate-checkout-`, `pup-gate-`) until the operator cleans `$TMPDIR` by hand. The ADR deliberately covers a failed rename, but a failed mkdtemp is a different case and it is not addressed.
findings.body:
**Cleanup stops freeing space once the temp volume is full.** `movedAside` now creates a fresh `pup-removing-*` directory before the rename ([sandbox.utils.ts#L562-L574](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/7167bf8ffc9375f2db65b1ca14c290afefb039f0/src/core/sandbox.utils.ts#L562-L574)):

```ts
const aside = mkdtempSync(join(dirname(path), 'pup-removing-'));
```

A new directory needs a free inode and a data block. On ext4, the reserved blocks are for root only, and APFS behaves the same way when its container is full. So for a regular user on a full volume, this `mkdir` fails with ENOSPC or EDQUOT. `unlink` and `rmdir`, which is all the old `rmSync` did, still succeed in that state.

The usual way the volume fills up is a gate child writing into its own scratch. That scratch is the run's `TMPDIR` (`pup-gate-`, line 618), and it is one of the paths this function removes. Here is what happens:

1. `endSandboxRun` calls `removeGateDir(run.scratchDir)`.
2. `lstatSync` succeeds, then `mkdtempSync` throws.
3. Because `left === path`, the catch prints `Could not remove … (ENOSPC); it is left behind.`. Nothing is freed.
4. The policy dir, the checkout root and the coverage holders go the same way.

pup has no sweep of stale `pup-*` temp dirs, so this space is not reclaimed by pup. The next `pup merge` then fails at its own `mkdtempSync` calls (lines 618/619, and `merge-gate.service.ts:1009`) until the operator cleans up by hand or the OS temp reaper runs. ADR 0155 covers a failed rename but not a failed `mkdtemp`. Before this PR, the same case cleaned up after itself.

Renaming `path` to a sibling name in the same parent (for example `join(dirname(path), `pup-removing-${randomBytes(8).toString('hex')}`)`) needs no new directory and is still covered by no grant, so the swap protection stays. The rename-back and the `left` bookkeeping would then follow that name. The other option is to record the ENOSPC/EDQUOT case as an accepted trade-off in ADR 0155.

findings.description: Trigger: `rmSync(moved)` succeeds, then `rmdirSync(dirname(moved))` throws (EBUSY, EPERM, or an entry in the aside directory). `left` is still `moved`, so `movedBack` tries `renameSync(moved, path)`. That fails with ENOENT because `moved` has already been deleted, and it returns `moved`. pup then prints "Could not remove <path> (EBUSY); it is left behind in <aside>/<name>." In fact `path` was fully removed, `<aside>/<name>` does not exist, and only an empty `pup-removing-*` directory is left. `movedBack` already treats a failed removal of the empty aside as not worth reporting, so the main path contradicts it. A rare trigger, but the message is wrong whenever it fires. Fix: set `left = path` after the `rmSync` and give the aside's `rmdirSync` its own swallowing `try`.

`rmSync` now receives the moved path (`…/pup-removing-X/pup-gate-checkout-Y`), so that is what `left` records. After the mocked ENOTEMPTY, `movedBack` renames the checkout back to `…/pup-gate-checkout-Y`. The `onTestFinished` cleanup then removes only the moved path, which no longer exists, and `force` hides that. Every run of this test therefore leaves a full gate worktree checkout in the system temp directory. Before this change `left[0]` was the real path and the cleanup removed it. The assertion already strips the `pup-removing-` segment; the cleanup should do the same, e.g. `removeForReal(path.replace(/\/pup-removing-[^/]+(?=\/)/, ''), …)`.
